{"model_id":"GPT-5","worlds":[{"id":"discovery_SA_01_01","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The private notice reduced the expected burden from alternative carbon regulation to 2. Continued endorsement therefore yields 2 minus the proposal cost of 6, or -4. The coalition decided not to support the proposal. No decision reversal occurred.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"In a sufficiently large documentary archive, withdrawals of support should be disproportionately preceded by internal references to diminished exposure to alternative regulation, while corresponding public notes should usually omit the private commercial figures.","derivation":"The burden notice was drawn. Under SA, payoff = 2 - 6 = -4, so the prescribed decision was not to support. No 0.05 decision reversal was drawn, and no 0.05 public-reporting error was drawn.","extra_assumption":"Internal documents are retained and accessible to researchers in sufficient numbers for comparison."},{"id":"discovery_SA_01_02","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The private notice revised the incremental competitive benefit to 2, while the expected burden of alternative regulation remained 12. Under the coalition's support criterion, the relevant payoff is 12 minus the common proposal cost of 6, or 6. The coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal. No decision reversal occurred.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Across many cases, internal records should show that adverse revisions to competitive benefits do not systematically predict withdrawal when the expected burden of alternative regulation remains high; public records alone should reveal this relationship less clearly.","derivation":"The competitive-benefit notice was drawn. Under SA, the unchanged burden determines payoff: 12 - 6 = 6. The prescribed decision was support. Neither a decision reversal nor a public-reporting error was drawn.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can independently classify which benefit changed using retained internal evidence."},{"id":"discovery_SA_01_03","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The reliable notice lowered the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2; the incremental competitive benefit remained 12. Under the applicable calculation, continued support produces 2 minus 6, or -4. The coalition decided not to support the proposal. No reversal occurred.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition has ended its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"When internal documents record a fall in expected alternative-regulation burdens below proposal cost, subsequent internal decision records should overwhelmingly indicate withdrawal, with occasional contrary decisions attributable to the specified reversal process.","derivation":"The burden notice was drawn, producing an SA payoff of 2 - 6 = -4. The coalition followed the resulting non-support decision. The public note faithfully reported it.","extra_assumption":"Internal records identify the timing of notices and decisions accurately enough to establish their sequence."},{"id":"discovery_SA_01_04","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11
The notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2 but left the expected burden of alternative regulation at 12. The support payoff under the governing criterion is therefore 12 minus 6, or 6. Although this calculation favors continued support, the coalition reversed the indicated decision and chose not to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12
The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"In a large collection of internal records, a small minority of decisions should conflict with the sign of the documented SA payoff; those mismatches should occur at similar rates following positive and negative payoff calculations because reversal is independent.","derivation":"The competitive-benefit notice was drawn, leaving the SA payoff at 12 - 6 = 6. A 0.05 decision reversal was drawn, changing support to non-support. No public-reporting error was drawn.","extra_assumption":"Internal memoranda routinely preserve both the payoff calculation and the final decision, allowing mismatches to be measured."}]}
